bugs.summary: AxiosError now extends Error and sets its message with super(message). The native Error constructor defines message as a non-enumerable own property, whereas the old function constructor assigned this.message = message (enumerable). So Object.keys(err), Object.entries(err), {...err} and for...in on an AxiosError no longer include message, silently breaking code that copies or logs errors that way.
bugs.trigger: const err = new AxiosError('Request failed', 'ERR_BAD_REQUEST'); Object.keys(err).includes('message') is true before this change and false after it; {...err}.message becomes undefined. The fix (#7392) redefines message with Object.defineProperty(this, 'message', {value: message, enumerable: true, writable: true, configurable: true}) and its message names this commit (v1.13.3) as the breaking change.

related_valid: AxiosError.from assigns axiosError.cause = error as a plain enumerable property, so JSON.stringify or a deep copy of the error walks into the original error and can hit circular structures (later fixed in #10913 by making cause non-enumerable).
status is now set to response.status even when it is undefined, where it used to be null.
AxiosError.from overwrites name with the wrapped error's name, so err.name may no longer be 'AxiosError'.
